# Fixture status: raw source only

The project contracts have not yet been approved. Consequently, this directory
currently contains only invented Yelp-shaped raw records and a minimal fixture
configuration. There are deliberately no prepared reviews, token outputs,
postings, ranking scores, PMI values, sentiment labels, or conforming provider
implementations yet.

## Current layout

```text
fixtures/
├── fixture.toml
├── raw/
│   ├── businesses.jsonl
│   └── reviews.jsonl
├── group_a/README.md
├── group_b/README.md
└── group_c/README.md
```

The raw fixture mirrors the source file shapes and covers conditions that are
likely to matter later: multiple categories and dates, an open and closed
business, an unmatched business reference, Unicode text, emoji, contractions,
hyphens, numbers, currency, repeated terms, and comparative language. These
records are test data, not a proposed downstream schema.

## What happens after contract approval

Each consuming group already has a reserved directory. It contains only a
status README until the relevant contracts are approved, after which inputs,
case labels, and mathematical oracles are added without mixing group concerns:

```text
fixtures/
├── raw/
├── group_a/
├── group_b/
└── group_c/
```

For every confirmed boundary, the interface owner must add together:

1. the approved contract under `src/yelptext/contracts/`;
2. a same-interface fake under `tests/fakes/`;
3. the smallest derived fixture covering normal and edge cases;
4. contract tests that run against both fake and real providers when the real
   provider becomes available.

Derived input may be generated reproducibly from `raw/`. Expected mathematical
outputs must be independently hand-checked rather than generated by the code
under test. Empirical choices such as tokenizer policy, thresholds, and query
quality still require a documented real-data sample.
